title: `@media not (width = 10px)` is printed as `@media (width = 10px)`

regression.commit: 7f29035 Compile media query range syntax with boolean logic instead of fractional pixels (2024-12-21)

impact: No reactions, no project named; part of the 2026-10-28 agent-style batch. `not (<feature> = <value>)` is rare in real CSS (equality on width/resolution is unusual, and negating it more so), but when hit the output silently applies the rule under the OPPOSITE condition, with or without minify and with any targets. Regression since 1.29.0 (2025-01-09). Not a duplicate: #1105/#1114 were about parenthesising lowered negations.
code: src/media_query.rs: QueryFeature::negate / MediaCondition::negate, used by MediaCondition::to_css for Not
summary: MediaCondition::to_css prints `not (range feature)` by inverting the comparison operator; MediaFeatureComparison::negate maps `=` to `=`, so the `not` is dropped and the query is inverted. Affects `not (width = 10px)`, `not (10px = width)`, `screen and (not (width = 10px))`, nested `(not (width = 10px)) and ...`, any feature (resolution, color), and the lowered form for old targets (`not (width = 10px)` -> `(width:10px)` for Safari 12). `@media not screen and (...)` (query qualifier) and `@container` are unaffected.
evidence: repro.mjs --range 1.28.0..1.33.0: 6 bug cases WRONG on 1.29.0..master, correct on 1.28.x; 3 controls correct throughout. Bisected release maps to 7f29035 (git blame of negate, tag v1.29.0 first containing it). Chromium equivalence (1396-fixture/in.css, --minify): NOT EQUIVALENT, `.a` red in input at every width but 10px, red only at 10px in output.

fix.approach: Make MediaFeatureComparison::negate return Option and return None for Equal (QueryFeature::negate then returns None, so to_css prints `not ` + the feature). Add tests for `not (width = 10px)`, the reversed form, nested, and with Safari 12 targets next to the `not (width < 240px)` tests in src/lib.rs.

draftReply:
Thanks, confirmed. Since 1.29.0, a negated range feature is printed by flipping its operator, and `=` has no opposite, so `@media not (width = 10px)` comes out as `@media (width=10px)` and the rule applies under the opposite condition. 1.28.2 kept the `not`. It affects any feature (`resolution`, `color`), the reversed `not (10px = width)` form, nested conditions, and the lowered output for older targets (`(width:10px)`). `@media not screen and (...)` and `@container` aren't affected.

The fix is to keep the `not` for equality instead of inverting it. Until then, writing the condition without `not`, e.g. `(width < 10px), (width > 10px)`, avoids it.
